title: Missed scheduled runs during downtime are buried in per-job history with no startup prompt or catch-up affordance
existing_state: On startup, RecordMissedSchedulerRunsOnStartup (Form1.cs:15258-15283) calls SchedulingService.DetectMissedRunSummaries (Services/SchedulingService.cs:148-181) and writes one skipped-run summary per affected job into that job's history file via SaveSkippedRunSummary — and nothing else. There is no dialog, banner, toast, or status-bar indication that runs were missed. The only way to discover that 'Nightly Backup' missed 5 runs while the laptop was off is to open the Job List dialog, select that specific job, and notice an orange 'Skipped' row in its history grid (JobListDialog.cs:690-693). Missed runs are never auto-executed by design (a reasonable policy), but the user is also never offered the choice, so the design intent ('inform the user') ends one click short of actually informing anyone.
recommendation: After RecordMissedSchedulerRunsOnStartup collects skippedSummaries (Form1.cs:15271-15274), if non-empty show a one-shot non-modal banner or themed dialog: 'While SSH Helper was closed, N scheduled runs were missed across M jobs' with a per-job list (name, missed count, last scheduled time) and buttons Run Now (per job, routing through existing RunTrackedJobNowAsync at Form1.cs:15311), Open Scheduler, and Dismiss. Cheapest credible version: a toast via the existing NotificationService plus a temporary status-bar suffix like 'Scheduler: 3 active (5 missed)'.
user_benefit: A user whose machine was off over the weekend immediately sees which maintenance jobs didn't run and can catch up with one click, instead of silently operating on stale device configs.

evidence.note: Detection result written to history only; no UI surface
DetectMissedRunSummaries aggregates missed occurrences per enabled recurring job
Skipped entries render orange only inside the selected job's history grid

mockup_idea: Startup banner strip under the menu bar: warning icon + '5 scheduled runs were missed while the app was closed (Nightly Backup x3, Cert Check x2)' with [Run missed jobs now] [Open Scheduler] [Dismiss] buttons; banner uses DialogTheme dark-mode colors.
